title: Price Lock, Escalation and Competitive Match Limits of the Contract Pricing Agreement Tiers
content:
**Price lock, escalation and competitive match limits — Contract Pricing Agreement**

Each tier fixes how long contract item prices are locked, how far and with how much notice a contract item may be escalated, and whether and how far a competitor's quote can be matched.

Columns, lowest tier to highest: **Account Price Schedule** = Corbett Account Price Schedule; **Volume Discount** = Corbett Volume Discount Agreement; **Category Contract** = Corbett Category Contract; **Net-Price** = Corbett Net-Price Contract; **Cost-Plus** = Corbett Cost-Plus Contract; **Strategic Supply** = Corbett Strategic Supply Agreement.

| Term | Account Price Schedule | Volume Discount | Category Contract | Net-Price | Cost-Plus | Strategic Supply |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price lock: months from the agreement effective date during which contract item prices cannot be escalated | 0 | 0 | 6 | 12 | 0 | 12 |
| Escalation cap: largest increase in one escalation, percent of the prior contract price | 0 | 0 | 4 | 3.5 | 0 | 3 |
| Escalation notice: calendar days between the notice date and the date an escalated price may take effect | 30 | 30 | 30 | 45 | 60 | 60 |
| Competitive match allowed on an existing contract item | No | No | Yes | Yes | No | Yes |
| Largest match reduction, percent of the current contract price | 0 | 0 | 5 | 8 | 0 | 10 |
| Largest age of the competitor's written quote on the date of the match request, calendar days | 30 | 30 | 30 | 45 | 45 | 60 |
| Lowest gross margin a matched price may carry, percent (price less supplier cost, over price) | 0 | 0 | 8 | 7 | 0 | 6 |

**Limit questions answered by the table**

- *Which tiers allow a competitive match?* Only the tiers whose row reads Yes: the Corbett Category Contract, the Corbett Net-Price Contract and the Corbett Strategic Supply Agreement.
- *Hypothetical cap reading:* under a 4 percent cap, a contract price of 10.0000 can rise by at most 4 percent of 10.0000, which is 0.4000, to 10.4000. (Illustrative figures.)
